name: CA Stochastic
miniText: How does uncertainty in a local transition change collective behavior? NetLogo CA Stochastic assigns a separate activation probability to each of the eight binary neighborhoods consisting of a cell and its immediate neighbors. Each generation is drawn as a new row, producing a one-dimensional space-time diagram. Wolfram [1] supplies the deterministic cellular foundation, Li and colleagues [2] study transitions across rule space, and Chaté and Manneville [3] analyze critical behavior. Setting probabilities to zero or one recovers deterministic cases, while intermediate values produce repeated runs with different realizations. Initial density, boundary conditions, and the eight probabilities jointly determine the observed patterns. The experiment illustrates stochastic update laws rather than merely uncertain initial conditions. A finite visual run cannot establish a critical point, a universal scaling law, or a faithful model of noisy natural processes.
